Show features: before and after

2026-09-29 · features 5 (viewer chaos), 9 (camera angles), 10 (season, cards, clips) and add-ons 4 (Unity Cloud), 8 (sound-pack import), 9 (Kenney art), 10 (training videos in TensorBoard)

Read this first. The "before" pictures were taken before the missing 3D model files were downloaded (they were Git LFS placeholders on this PC), so the grey sky and stick figures in them are not part of this change. Everything boxed in orange is new. All pictures are real editor captures; they were squeezed to 1280×720 by the capture tool and are stretched back to the phone's shape here.

1 · Race screen: viewer buttons

Before

After

  1. New button row: GUST (a crosswind across the deck), SHOVE (a push on the leader), SLICK (a wet patch ahead of the leader), and the camera picker (AUTO → DRONE → HEAD → RAIL). Each button greys out and counts down for 5 s after use.
  2. Name strip moved up one row so the new buttons do not cover it.

2 · Results card: points, bests, season, clip

Before

After

  1. Decathlon points per runner, from the official World Athletics formula (see section 5 for how the AI times are converted).
  2. Star = personal best in this event.
  3. Season table: top five totals, how many events are done, and what is next.
  4. Highlight clip saved: the last 6 seconds up to the finish, as a GIF on the device.
  5. NEXT: LONG JUMP replaces RACE AGAIN while a season is running.

3 · Setup menu: season and athlete cards

Before

After

  1. CARDS opens every athlete’s record. START SEASON runs all five events in decathlon order with the field above (it becomes CONTINUE SEASON 2/5 … once one is running). The athlete tiles shrank slightly to make room.

4 · The new pictures NEW

5 · What was measured

CheckResult
Everything compilesYes, no new warnings.
Gust, shove, wet patch fire in a live raceYes. Wet patch placed on the deck with friction 0.3. The commentary calls each one.
Did the buttons make runners fall?Not measurably. A control race with no buttons pressed had 7 of 8 fall (at 3–22 m); the race with all three fired had 8 of 8 fall but further on (24–29 m). This field falls a lot on its own. One race each is not proof either way.
Camera pickerDRONE, HEAD, RAIL all cut in; the first head-cam test showed the inside of the runner's head, fixed (lens moved forward, near clip 0.2 m) and re-checked.
PointsMatt RL 1, 31.0 s → 178–183 pts. Long jump 2.50 m → 642 pts. The 100 m scale is set so the reference lap of 24.2 s scores 699; the other four events' conversion factors are first guesses.
Season hand-offNEXT carried the season's 4-athlete field into the long jump and scored it as event 2 of 3.
Highlight clipSaved every race: 72 frames, 172×480, loops, overlay included, about 2 MB.
Unity CloudSigns in and saves. Leaderboard posts reach the server and are refused with “Leaderboard config could not be found”: the six boards still need creating in the dashboard.
Sound-pack importerOn a generated test pack: 14 slots filled, decoys rejected, 400 ms of silence trimmed to 2 ms, peaks at −3 dB. Not yet run on the real Sonniss bundle (not downloaded).
Training videosOn a test checkpoint: 6 s clip rendered in about 5 s, visible in TensorBoard under rollout/<task>. Not yet run inside a real training run.
